transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because... for a while now, I’ve been pretty convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. Which is a lot of clients, you know, since I'm a financial advisor. I actually just had a meeting with one yesterday down in Over-the-Rhine at this little coffee shop. They do this amazing pour-over coffee there—takes like ten minutes to make, which is kind of annoying when you're in a rush, and don't even get me started on the parking down there with all the construction on Liberty Street. I had to circle the block three times just to find a meter. 

But anyway, yeah, I've noticed these people are sending me little signals. Through, like, event invitations, or the topics they choose for panels, or even who ends up sitting right next to me at these networking dinners. Like this one guy last month was seated next to me wearing a full velvet blazer, which... who wears velvet in the spring? It was navy blue, too. Just a really strange wardrobe choice if you ask me. But... yeah, even when I tell myself that all of this, the signals and the seating and the invitations, could just be a coincidence, I just... I can’t really let it go. It's just stuck in my head.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or when no one was around?

No, no voices or anything like that. I mean, it's mostly just regular noise around me, you know? Like the trash trucks. Oh man, the trash trucks in my neighborhood come at like 4:30 in the morning on Tuesdays and it is just *so* loud. I actually tried talking to the building manager about it, because I'm on the second floor and my bedroom window faces the alley. He told me to just buy earplugs, which, honestly, is just terrible management. 

I pay way too much in HOA fees to be dismissed like that. They just raised the dues by 15% this year, too, and for what? They haven't even fixed the water fountain in the main courtyard. It's just been sitting there completely empty since October, just collecting dead leaves and trash. It looks terrible, especially if I have to bring a client by my home office for a quick signature or something. First impressions really matter in wealth management, you know? You can't just have a dry, dirty fountain as the first thing people see when they're trusting you with their retirement accounts.
How has your sleep been recently?

My sleep? Um, I guess it's been okay. I haven't really noticed any major issues with it, besides those trash trucks, obviously. But I did buy a new mattress a couple of months ago, actually. It's one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box. It's wild how they manage to compress a whole king-size mattress into a box that fits in the hallway. The delivery guy just left it downstairs, though, which was super annoying because getting it up the stairs by myself was a nightmare. I almost knocked over Mrs. Higgins' potted fern on the landing. She’s my neighbor across the hall, and she is extremely particular about her plants. She leaves passive-aggressive notes in the mailroom if anyone even brushes past them. Like, last week she left a note about someone leaving a grocery store receipt on the floor, and I'm pretty sure it was directed at me because I shop at Kroger and the receipt had a Kroger logo on it. But I always put my receipts in my wallet, so I don't even know why she'd think that. People are just so quick to jump to conclusions, you know?

Doctor: How long have you been feeling like people in the arts and finance circles are tracking your meetings and sending you signals?

Patient: Oh, the tracking thing? Um, I'd say it's been going on for about two months now. Yeah, right around the time I went to that gallery opening downtown. It was this contemporary photography exhibit, mostly black and white prints of industrial architecture. Really stark, kind of moody stuff. I actually ended up buying a small piece for my office, just a shot of an old steel bridge, because I thought it would look good above the filing cabinet. But getting it framed was a whole ordeal. I took it to this custom framing place in Oakley, and the guy working there was just incredibly slow. He spent like twenty minutes just showing me different shades of matte board—like, eggshell, ivory, bone. They all looked exactly the same to me! And then he tried to upsell me on this museum-quality UV-protective glass that cost more than the actual photograph. I mean, my office doesn't even get direct sunlight, the blinds are always drawn because the glare on my computer monitor gives me a headache by 3 PM. I've been meaning to ask maintenance to install those anti-glare screen covers, but you know how they are. If it's not an emergency, you're at the bottom of the list. Just like the water fountain.
During these past two months, how has your mood been overall?

My mood? I mean, it's fine, I guess. I haven't really been too down or anything. Maybe just a little stressed with work, but that's normal. Actually, speaking of work, I had this client come in yesterday—Mr. Abernathy, older guy, retired dentist—and he insisted on bringing his dog into the office. It’s this little yappy terrier thing, and it just would not stop barking at the copier. Every time it printed a page, the dog went nuts. I tried to offer it a treat from the jar I keep on my desk, but Mr. Abernathy said it’s on a strict grain-free diet because of its allergies. Which, I mean, fine, but he spent twenty minutes explaining the dog's digestive issues instead of looking over the portfolio rebalancing I’d prepared for him. And I had spent hours on that! The market’s been so volatile lately, especially with tech stocks, and I really wanted to make sure he was positioned defensively. But no, we had to talk about hypoallergenic dog food. I actually saw a documentary about the pet food industry on Netflix last weekend. It’s crazy how unregulated some of it is. They just put whatever filler they want in there and slap a premium label on it. Kind of like how they market some of these mutual funds, honestly. Just a bunch of junk bundled together with a fancy name and a high expense ratio.

I made a frozen pizza in it the other night, and it actually turned out pretty good. The crust got perfectly crispy. Way better than the microwave, obviously. Microwaved pizza is just sad.

Are you asking how long this has been going on? Um, yeah, these changes, the feeling that they're tracking me, it's been building since I got that recognition from the arts nonprofit. That was a little over two years ago. I actually still have the plaque they gave me on my desk. It's made of this really heavy glass, or maybe it's crystal? Have you ever felt like you have a special ability to sense things before they happen, or that you can communicate with others without speaking?

Communicate without speaking? No, no, nothing like telepathy or seeing the future. Though I really wish I could predict the future sometimes, especially with the market the way it is right now. My clients are always asking me to basically look into a crystal ball. Like this one guy I work with, Richard, he kept insisting on moving a huge chunk of his retirement portfolio into this start-up that makes fitness trackers for dogs. Like a smartwatch, but for a golden retriever. I tried to tell him it was a terrible idea, but he wouldn't listen. 

He actually has a golden retriever himself, Barnaby, who is just massively overweight. I saw him trying to walk Barnaby at the park last week, and the dog just laid down right in the middle of the playground mulch and completely refused to budge. That mulch is terrible, by the way. It’s those huge, cheap, jagged wood chips that get stuck in your shoes and give you splinters. The city really ought to replace it with that soft, recycled rubber flooring. They put that in at the park near my sister’s place up in Columbus, and it’s so much nicer. Plus, it doesn't wash away every time it rains. It rained so hard yesterday, my gutters completely overflowed again. I'm pretty sure they're clogged with oak leaves, but my ladder is too short to reach the second story, so I'm going to have to hire someone to come out and clean them. It's always something with homeownership, you know?

Outside of my family? Um, well, friends try to check in and ask what's going on, but I just give them really short answers. Honestly, talking just feels like way more effort than it should be lately. I just don't have the same spark, you know? I’ve been skipping out on my usual stuff, like jazz nights or pickup basketball, and I don't even really feel anything about missing it. 

I used to go to the rec center every Thursday for hoops. Though, honestly, the court there is a disaster. They never wax the floors, so you just slide everywhere. I actually bought these special grip shoes online to help with it, but the delivery driver kept taking them to the wrong building. My apartment complex has the worst numbering system. There's a Building 4 and a Building 4A, and they aren't even next to each other. They’re separated by this huge retention pond that gets absolutely infested with mosquitoes in July. You can't even walk to your car without getting bit. The property management refuses to spray for them because they say it hurts the local bee population, which I guess I understand, but still, it makes walking outside miserable. 

But yeah, it’s not just basketball and friends. Even at work, I still get things done in pieces, but I'll just leave client follow-ups sitting there on my desk. I just don't have the drive for it right now.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about magical thinking, telepathy, or clairvoyance (feeling a special ability to sense things before they happen or communicate without speaking), which are symptoms often assessed for schizotypal personality disorder. My symptom profile covers delusions, negative symptoms, functional impairment, and duration, but does not include magical thinking or telepathy.

patient.answer:
Communicate without speaking? No, no, nothing like telepathy or seeing the future. Though I really wish I could predict the future sometimes, especially with the market the way it is right now. My clients are always asking me to basically look into a crystal ball. Like this one guy I work with, Richard, he kept insisting on moving a huge chunk of his retirement portfolio into this start-up that makes fitness trackers for dogs. Like a smartwatch, but for a golden retriever. I tried to tell him it was a terrible idea, but he wouldn't listen. 

He actually has a golden retriever himself, Barnaby, who is just massively overweight. I saw him trying to walk Barnaby at the park last week, and the dog just laid down right in the middle of the playground mulch and completely refused to budge. That mulch is terrible, by the way. It’s those huge, cheap, jagged wood chips that get stuck in your shoes and give you splinters. The city really ought to replace it with that soft, recycled rubber flooring. They put that in at the park near my sister’s place up in Columbus, and it’s so much nicer. Plus, it doesn't wash away every time it rains. It rained so hard yesterday, my gutters completely overflowed again. I'm pretty sure they're clogged with oak leaves, but my ladder is too short to reach the second story, so I'm going to have to hire someone to come out and clean them. It's always something with homeownership, you know?

inference.note: Initial assessment based on over two years of referential and suspicious thinking, prominent circumstantial speech, and absence of overt hallucinations or thought alienation.

patient.answer:
Outside of my family? Um, well, friends try to check in and ask what's going on, but I just give them really short answers. Honestly, talking just feels like way more effort than it should be lately. I just don't have the same spark, you know? I’ve been skipping out on my usual stuff, like jazz nights or pickup basketball, and I don't even really feel anything about missing it. 

I used to go to the rec center every Thursday for hoops. Though, honestly, the court there is a disaster. They never wax the floors, so you just slide everywhere. I actually bought these special grip shoes online to help with it, but the delivery driver kept taking them to the wrong building. My apartment complex has the worst numbering system. There's a Building 4 and a Building 4A, and they aren't even next to each other. They’re separated by this huge retention pond that gets absolutely infested with mosquitoes in July. You can't even walk to your car without getting bit. The property management refuses to spray for them because they say it hurts the local bee population, which I guess I understand, but still, it makes walking outside miserable. 

But yeah, it’s not just basketball and friends. Even at work, I still get things done in pieces, but I'll just leave client follow-ups sitting there on my desk. I just don't have the drive for it right now.
